title: Establishment and Morphological Characterization of Patient-Derived Organoids from Breast Cancer
author: Mazzucchelli, Piccotti, et al.
materials: Human breast primary tumor tissue from surgical specimen or from biopsy (fresh; the quantity usually varies).

In the reference period, fresh tumor specimens from surgical resections have been collected from 24 patients affected by breast cancer at any stage and candidated to immediate breast-conserving surgery or total mastectomy. A written and oral informed consent to participate in the present protocol was obtained from each patient. Tumor specimens obtained from surgical resection could be stored at 4 °C in working medium (WM) until processing. Processing into organoids should be performed in sterile conditions within 48 h from the day of collection. All tissue processing was performed in a biosafety cabinet (hood) using Biosafety Level 2 (BSL2) techniques. steps.title: Prepare surgical tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the solid tumor specimen to a 6 cm or 10 cm sterile petri dish, keep it moist with PBS, trim away visible fat, mince the tissue with a scalpel using a criss‑cross motion, weigh the minced tissue, and transfer it to a pre‑weighed 50 mL sterile tube using a cell lifter.

steps.title: Digest surgical tissue
steps.instruction: Add digestion buffer at 10 mL per gram of tissue (DMEM‑F/12 supplemented with 10 mM HEPES, 2 % BSA, 0.5 µg mL⁻¹ hydrocortisone, 50 µg mL⁻¹ gentamicin) together with Collagenase III (Wortington #LS004182; 0.2 mg mL⁻¹) and Hyaluronidase (Sigma #H3884; 1000 U mL⁻¹). Incubate 16 h at 37 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.

steps.title: Filter digested tissue
steps.instruction: Pass the digestion mixture through a sterile 100 µm cell strainer into a new 50 mL tube; the flow‑through contains PDO, single cancer cells, red blood cells and fat.

steps.title: Separate organoids with 20 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Place a sterile 20 µm cell strainer on a fresh 50 mL tube (label as “single cells fraction”), discard the 100 µm strainer, and load the collected flow‑through onto the 20 µm strainer. Wash the strainer twice with 5 mL of WM (working medium) to collect organoids retained on the grid.

steps.title: Collect organoid pellet
steps.instruction: Discard the 20 µm strainer, centrifuge the organoid suspension 5 min at 500 × g, 8 °C, and carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Remove red blood cells (if present)
steps.instruction: If a red layer is visible, add 1 mL TAC buffer, incubate 10 min at 37 °C water bath, then neutralize with 10 mL WM and centrifuge again 5 min at 500 × g, 8 °C.

steps.title: Remove excess fat (if present)
steps.instruction: If the pellet contains a lot of fat, wash the pellet one or two additional times with 10 mL WM, centrifuging each time as above.

steps.title: Resuspend organoids in Matrigel
steps.instruction: Remove supernatant, resuspend the organoid pellet in Matrigel 90 % (Matrigel mixed with WM, Corning #356231). Use the volumes from Table 1 (e.g., 150 µL per well for 6‑well, 70 µL for 12‑well, 35 µL for 24‑well). If the pellet is invisible, seed directly into a 24‑well well.

steps.title: Seed Matrigel drops
steps.instruction: Place the Matrigel‑organoid mixture as drops in a pre‑warmed multi‑well plate, invert the plate to prevent sinking, incubate 10 min at room temperature, then transfer the plate to a 37 °C incubator for 20 min to allow solidification.

steps.title: Prepare and add CCM
steps.instruction: While Matrigel solidifies, prepare Complete Culture Medium (CCM). After solidification, invert the plate, gently add CCM to each drop (volumes from Table 2: 1.5–2 mL per well for 6‑well, 1 mL for 12‑well, 0.5 mL for 24‑well), and return the plate to the incubator for culture.

steps.title: Prepare biopsy tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer a fresh breast cancer core‑biopsy (≈1.5 × 20 × 1.5 mm) into sterile WM, keep moist with PBS, mince with a scalpel (criss‑cross), and transfer the minced tissue to a pre‑weighed 15 mL tube using a cell lifter.

steps.title: Digest biopsy tissue
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL digestion buffer (DMEM‑F/12 + 10 mM HEPES, 2 % BSA, 0.5 µg mL⁻¹ hydrocortisone, 50 µg mL⁻¹ gentamicin) with Collagenase III (0.2 mg mL⁻¹) and Hyaluronidase (1000 U mL⁻¹). Incubate 3–4 h at 37 °C, 200 rpm.

steps.title: Filter and wash biopsy digest
steps.instruction: Filter the digest through a 100 µm cell strainer, collect the flow‑through, wash the strainer with 5 mL WM, repeat the filtration step once more, then centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, 8 °C. Discard supernatant.

steps.title: RBC/fat removal for biopsy
steps.instruction: If red blood cells are present, resuspend pellet in 1 mL TAC buffer, incubate 10 min at 37 °C, neutralize with 10 mL WM, centrifuge as above. If excess fat is observed, wash once with 10 mL WM.

steps.title: Embed biopsy organoids in Matrigel
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in Matrigel 90 % (same Matrigel product as above) using Table 1 volumes, seed, invert, solidify (10 min + 20 min at 37 °C), and add CCM as described in steps 9‑10.

steps.title: Passage organoids – expansion (no shearing)
steps.instruction: To expand cultures without shearing: dissolve Matrigel drops with remaining CCM, transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube, wash the plate twice with fresh WM (≥2 mL per well), collect washes, centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, 8 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 90 % Matrigel at a 1:2–1:3 dilution, seed drops, invert, solidify (10 min + 20 min), prepare CCM and add the appropriate volume (Table 2).

steps.title: Passage organoids – shearing with TrypLE
steps.instruction: To passage compact organoids: dissolve Matrigel with CCM, transfer to a 15 mL tube, wash plate twice with WM, collect washes, centrifuge as above, discard supernatant leaving 1 mL WM, add 1 mL TrypLE (WM:TrypLE = 1:1), pipette up‑and‑down 20 times with a flame‑sterilized glass Pasteur, examine under a light microscope; if organoids are not ruptured, continue pipetting 10–15 more times. Neutralize with 10 mL WM, centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, 8 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 90 % Matrigel (1:2–1:3), seed drops, invert, solidify (10 min + 20 min), prepare CCM and add as above.

steps.title: Cryopreserve organoids
steps.instruction: When organoids are dense (40–100 µm) in a 6‑well plate: dissolve Matrigel with CCM, transfer to a 15 mL tube, wash plate twice with fresh WM (≥2 mL per well), centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, 8 °C, discard supernatant leaving 1 mL WM, add 1 mL TrypLE (1:1), pipette 20 times, check under microscope and repeat pipetting if needed, neutralize with 10 mL WM, centrifuge, discard supernatant, resuspend in 90 % Matrigel, seed back into a 6‑well plate, invert, solidify (10 min + 20 min), add CCM and incubate. After 2 days, dissolve Matrigel with CCM, transfer to pre‑chilled 15 mL tubes (use two tubes per full 6‑well), keep on ice, wash plate twice with ice‑cold WM, centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, 8 °C, discard supernatant leaving 1 mL WM, add 11 mL ice‑cold WM, incubate 10 min on ice, pipette up‑and‑down, centrifuge again, discard supernatant and repeat washing 18–20 times if the suspension exceeds 0.2 mL. Keep tubes on ice, add 3 mL freezing medium to each tube, aliquot 0.5 mL into cryovials (six aliquots per tube), place vials in a Nalgene Cryostep for 24 h at –80 °C, then transfer to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Thaw and re‑plate organoids
steps.instruction: One day before thawing, pre‑warm a 24‑well plate in the incubator and pre‑warm WM to 37 °C. Thaw a cryovial rapidly in a 37 °C water bath with agitation until a small frozen piece remains, then wipe the outside with ethanol in a biosafety cabinet. Transfer the contents to a sterile 15 mL Falcon tube, add 1 mL warm WM drop‑wise while gently shaking, pipette a few times, then add 9 mL warm WM, invert the tube, centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, 8 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in ~70 µL of 90 % Matrigel (the same volume that was frozen), seed the suspension into the pre‑warmed 24‑well plate, invert, incubate 10 min then 20 min at 37 °C for solidification, add CCM, and culture. Monitor growth for several days to confirm successful recovery.

steps.title: Stain PDO for histology
steps.instruction: Remove CCM from the plate, incubate organoid drops with 0.05 % crystal violet for 30 min, then wash three times with PBS.

steps.title: Embed PDO in agarose
steps.instruction: Prepare 2 % agarose by boiling agarose in milliQ water. Place a labelled PDO drop (using a cell lifter) into a 15 × 15 × 5 mm mold pre‑filled with unsolidified 2 % agarose, add 3–4 additional Matrigel drops, and allow the agarose to solidify for ~15 min. Remove the agarose block, orient it in a histology cassette, and fix in 10 % buffered formalin.

steps.title: Dehydrate, clear and embed in paraffin
steps.instruction: Using a HistoStar embedding workstation (Leica ASP300): after 2 h fixation in 10 % formalin, dehydrate through 95 % ethanol (3 × 1 h + 1 × 2 h), then absolute ethanol (2 × 1 h + 1 × 2 h), clear in Bioclear (2 × 1 h + 1 × 2 h), and embed in paraffin wax (2 × 1 h + 1 × 2 h).

steps.title: Cut and label IHC slides
steps.instruction: Section the paraffin‑embedded PDO at 3.5 µm, mount on slides, and perform automated IHC on a VENTANA BenchMark ULTRA for E‑cadherin, HER2 (c‑ErbB2), estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and Ki‑67 using the antibody clones listed in Table 3. After IHC, counter‑stain with eosin, dehydrate (95 % ethanol 2 ×, 100 % ethanol 2 ×), clear in Bioclear, and mount with a coverslip.

steps.title: Prepare organoids for TEM
steps.instruction: Remove a PDO drop from Matrigel with a cell lifter into a 1.5 mL tube, add 1 mL 2.5 % glutaraldehyde in cacodylate buffer and incubate overnight. Wash three times with cacodylate buffer, then fix with 1.5 % osmium tetroxide in cacodylate buffer for 2 h. Wash again, dehydrate through an ethanol ladder (50 % → 100 %), embed in epon, cut ultrathin sections (70–80 nm), stain with uranyl acetate and lead citrate, and image on a Tecnai Spirit BT (FEI) transmission electron microscope.
